title: Semantic Chunking
shortDefinition: A document splitting strategy that divides content into chunks based on semantic meaning and topic boundaries.
definition: Semantic chunking is a document splitting strategy for RAG systems that divides content into chunks based on semantic meaning and topic boundaries — keeping related ideas together — rather than splitting at fixed character or word counts, which can cut sentences or concepts mid-thought regardless of content coherence. The quality of a RAG system's chunking strategy directly affects retrieval quality: poor chunking produces chunks missing essential context or combining unrelated concepts, leading to worse retrieval and ultimately worse generated answers even with a capable LLM.

sections.title: Fixed-size vs. semantic chunking: the core tradeoff
sections.description: Fixed-size chunking is simple but ignores structure; semantic chunking keeps related content together.

content.text: Fixed-size chunking (splitting every N characters or words) is simple to implement and predictable, but ignores content structure — it will routinely split mid-sentence, separate a question from its answer, or combine the end of one topic with the beginning of another into a single chunk. Semantic chunking uses content signals (sentence boundaries, paragraph breaks, section headers, topic coherence measured by embedding similarity) to find natural split points that keep semantically related content together. The tradeoff is complexity: semantic chunking is more sophisticated to implement and tune, but produces chunks that are more coherent units of meaning for the retrieval system to work with.

content.title: The key insight
content.text: Semantic chunking produces chunks that are coherent units of meaning — poor chunking is often the hidden cause of disappointing RAG quality.

sections.title: Why chunking strategy is often the biggest RAG quality lever

content.text: In a RAG system, retrieved chunks become the context from which the LLM generates its answer — if the retrieved chunks cut off mid-explanation or mix unrelated content, the LLM is working from incomplete or confused source material regardless of how capable the model is. Many teams debugging poor RAG answer quality focus on model selection or prompt engineering while the actual problem is chunking producing chunks that don't contain the complete, self-contained information needed to answer the query. Improving chunking strategy is often the highest-leverage RAG quality improvement available and one of the first things ClickMasters examines when auditing underperforming RAG systems.

sections.title: Limitations and risks of semantic chunking

content.text: Semantic chunking has limitations. It is more complex to implement and tune than fixed-size chunking. Content signals may be inconsistent across documents, making automatic splitting difficult. Over-chunking can create too many small, semantically similar chunks that confuse retrieval. Under-chunking creates large chunks that may contain too much information for the context window or dilute specific content. The optimal chunking strategy depends on the specific content type and may need to be adapted for different document types. Chunking optimization requires validation to confirm improvement.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions about semantic chunking

items.question: What chunk size should we use for our RAG system?
items.answer: This depends on your content type, embedding model, and context window; ClickMasters validates chunk size through retrieval quality measurement on your actual content rather than applying a generic default.

items.question: Does chunking strategy affect how many tokens the RAG system uses per query?
items.answer: Yes — chunk size determines how much context each retrieved chunk provides, affecting the total tokens in each RAG prompt and therefore per-query cost.

items.question: Can different document types in the same RAG system use different chunking strategies?
items.answer: Yes, and this is often the right approach — legal documents, support tickets, and product documentation each have different natural structure that benefits from tailored chunking strategies.

items.question: How do you measure whether a new chunking strategy actually improves retrieval?
items.answer: Through retrieval quality metrics (precision@k, recall) comparing the same queries before and after the chunking change — ClickMasters validates this rather than assuming improvement.

items.question: How long does chunking optimization take?
items.answer: 6–16 weeks depending on content type diversity and whether it's optimization of an existing system or new development.

items.question: Is chunking only relevant for text documents, or also for structured data?
items.answer: Primarily text documents in RAG applications; structured data typically doesn't need chunking since it can be queried directly rather than through semantic retrieval.

items.question: What is a chunk in RAG systems?
items.answer: A chunk is a segment of text from a source document that is stored in the vector database and retrieved as context for the LLM. The chunking strategy determines how documents are divided into these retrievable units.

items.question: What is the difference between character-based and semantic chunking?
items.answer: Character-based chunking splits at fixed character counts regardless of content. Semantic chunking splits at natural boundaries (paragraphs, sections, topic changes) to keep related content together. Semantic chunking produces more coherent retrieval units.

items.question: How does chunking affect RAG cost?
items.answer: Chunking affects both retrieval and generation cost. Larger chunks may contain more relevant content but also increase token count. Smaller chunks may require retrieving more chunks to answer a query. ClickMasters balances these tradeoffs for your use case.

items.question: Can chunking be combined with overlapping?
items.answer: Yes — overlapping chunks keep context continuity by including some content from neighboring chunks. This helps ensure that content near boundaries is not lost. ClickMasters designs appropriate overlap strategies for your content.
